transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-19
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Jared Liu (SummitWorks Procurement), Sara Kim (SummitWorks Security), Tom Reyes (SummitWorks Head of Eng)

Summary (auto): procurement review of MSA/DPA, SLAs, security artifacts; clarifying data residency and KMS; pricing approval path and PO timing; onboarding steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time, uh, really appreciate it. quick intros?
[00:08] Jared Liu: Jared here, procurement at SummitWorks. we'll be handling the contract review and PO.
[00:12] Sara Kim: Sara, security lead. i'll be reviewing SOC2, data flows, KMS, encryption, that side.
[00:18] Tom Reyes: Tom, head of engineering. i'll be the technical owner for the pilot and benchmarks.
[00:22] Ethan Cole: Ethan from Redwood, solutions engineering, i'll handle the technical runbook and benchmark template.
[00:28] Maya Patel: Great. agenda — walk through MSA and DPA redlines you flagged, SLA questions, SSO/KMS and security artifacts, then pricing and onboarding timeline.
[00:40] Jared Liu: Yeah we have three main things: 1) can we get MSA redlines, especially liability and indemnity language; 2) data residency & DPA clarifications; 3) pricing approvals — need a ballpark to route to finance.
[01:05] Maya Patel: Totally. on the MSA we'll send our standard redlines but we're fine talking through specific clauses. indemnity — we typically have mutual indemnity with carve-outs for willful misconduct. does that align with your legal team's must-haves?
[01:20] Jared Liu: Their ask was more provider liability cap tied to fees. can we consider a staggered cap for pilot vs production? legal tends to push for clarity here.
[01:32] Ethan Cole: from a delivery standpoint we can do pilot-limited caps; production commitments would be under the Dedicated contract or enterprise addendum.
[01:40] Sara Kim: on DPA, we need to confirm export controls and data residency — all PHI-inferred data must stay in US datacenter. do you support region pinning and customer-managed KMS?
[01:54] Ethan Cole: yes, region pinning is supported in Redwood Private; for hosted we have region controls and VPC options for Private deployments. customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported for Private deployments; for hosted we offer KMS integration via our key wrap and can discuss bring-your-own-key options.
[02:12] Tom Reyes: For the pilot, we plan to send a subset of de-identified records but we need assurance of KV cache handling and retention. what's retention defaults on caching?
[02:23] Ethan Cole: default KV cache TTL is 24 hours in our hosted default; we can adjust or disable prefix caching per customer policy. also full audit logs available for request/response metadata.
[02:34] Sara Kim: Audit logs — do you provide token-level tracing and redact PII automatically? we need proof of PII handling and redact controls.
[02:45] Ethan Cole: we provide token-level cost and latency traces; PII redaction is not automatic across all models — we recommend a pre-processing step. but we do have redaction tools and can run a PII detection pipeline as part of onboarding. we also have enterprise data masking options.
[02:58] Jared Liu: about SOC2 — do you have Type II and can you share the report and pen test summary? procurement will need that with the DPA.
[03:07] Maya Patel: yes we have SOC2 Type II, we will share our security pack including pen test summary and controls matrix. we'll also include our ISO statement and KMS architecture doc.
[03:17] Tom Reyes: ok, good. pricing — we need a simple figure to present. are you going to send the pricing schedule? and any discount for committed monthly for Dedicated?
[03:27] Maya Patel: i'll send the pricing sheet. committed reserved capacity for Dedicated comes with tiered discounts; for the pilot we can offer a discounted pilot rate. i can put numbers in the sheet and a recommended commit level.
[03:36] Jared Liu: timing — procurement needs about two weeks for legal review typically, finance another week for PO. can you get the redlines and security pack to us by end of next week?
[03:47] Maya Patel: yes, target send by 2026-10-22. is that ok?
[03:50] Jared Liu: yes that would work.
[03:52] [05:00] Ethan Cole: (technical clarifications) for the benchmark template — we usually request sample traffic distribution, max seq length, expected QPS and latency SLOs. tom if you can give us a baseline we'll produce expected throughput and cost estimates.
[05:20] Tom Reyes: expected QPS around 10 for pilot, burst to 50; typical prompt avg tokens 180, responses average 120. latency target was under 300ms p50, p95 under 800ms.
[05:36] Ethan Cole: noted. that'll inform batching and quantization recommendations. for on-prem / private we can hit lower p95s with dedicated GPUs and optimized kernels.
[05:48] Sara Kim: can you confirm data wipe policy for decommed instances? we need certifyable erase.
[05:55] Ethan Cole: yes, we support certified data wipe procedures and will provide attestation for Private deployments. for Hosted we have retention policies and can provide logs; for Private we can do full wipe with proof.
[06:10] Jared Liu: what about SLAs? uptime and credits — procurement wants an SLA that aligns with our SRE targets; typical ask is 99.9% with credit structure.
[06:22] Maya Patel: we can offer SLA tiers; hosted default is 99.5% but Dedicated enterprise contracts can go to 99.9% with financial credits and incident response SLAs. we'll include proposed SLA language in the MSA redline package.
[06:35] Jared Liu: do you have examples of credit calculations?
[06:37] Maya Patel: yes, we have standard language — e.g., 5% service credit for monthly availability between 99.0%-99.5%, 10% for lower. we'll attach the SLA schedule.
[06:48] [10:12] Tom Reyes: just to be clear on the onboarding steps — once contracts are signed, what's the standard timeline to have pilot infra up?
[10:22] Ethan Cole: typical onboarding is 2 weeks to provision and run initial benchmarks for hosted; Private can take 4-6 weeks depending on networking and KMS integrations. pilot can start earlier with containerized test harness.
[10:34] Jared Liu: our ideal timeline is sign by mid-November and pilot by end of November. is that realistic?
[10:39] Maya Patel: yes, if legal moves in the 2 week window and finance issues PO, we can hit that.
[10:45] Sara Kim: one more security item — SSO. we require SAML SSO to integrate with Okta and role-based access. do you support SCIM for provisioning?
[10:56] Ethan Cole: yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync and RBAC. we'll include admin setup docs.
[11:05] Jared Liu: ok great. any concerns from Redwood side about the DPA redlines we sent earlier?
[11:12] Maya Patel: we reviewed them — the main asks are around subprocessor lists and security obligations. we can accept most of the language but will propose small edits for operational clarity.
[11:22] Tom Reyes: about subprocessors, can you provide the full list and notify on changes? we need at least 30 days notice.
[11:30] Ethan Cole: yes, we publish an updated subprocessor list and provide notification windows; we'll add that to the DPA.
[11:36] [15:00] Maya Patel: quick recap — we'll do: send redlined MSA/DPA + SLA schedule, pricing sheet, security pack (SOC2 Type II + pen test summary), and pilot SOW and benchmark template. target send by 10/22.
[15:20] Jared Liu: procurement will aim to review the MSA within 7 business days; legal may request follow ups. finance will need pricing to route PO.
[15:30] Sara Kim: security will review SOC2 and pen test; may ask for additional controls or attestation.
[15:40] Tom Reyes: engineering will review the benchmark template once we get it; i'll coordinate with Ethan on specific metrics and test data.
[15:50] Maya Patel: any blockers we haven't covered?
[15:53] Jared Liu: no blockers, just need to get documents to legal and security.
[15:58] Ethan Cole: i'll draft the benchmark runbook and include the KV/cache retention options and instructions to disable caching for the pilot.
[16:06] Maya Patel: perfect. we'll also include the onboarding calendar options — 2 week hosted baseline or 4-6 week private onboarding.
[16:15] Jared Liu: one last ask — will you provide a short RACI or support escalation path as part of the SOW? procurement likes that.
[16:22] Maya Patel: yes we'll include RACI and incident escalation contacts in the SOW.
[16:28] [20:00] (crosstalk)
[20:10] Maya Patel: alright folks, i'll follow up via email with the package. thanks for your time.
[20:15] Jared Liu: thanks, appreciate it.
[20:18] Sara Kim: thanks everyone.
[20:20] Tom Reyes: thanks.

End of meeting.

Notes: transcription contains a few automatic mismatches (names, acronyms) — treat timestamps as approximate.
